beats.text: Hello everyone. In this video, I'll walk you through ToolTrace.
ToolTrace keeps track of every tool in your factory, and its calibration, in one simple app.
It is built for the tool crib, the shop floor and the quality team. It works on a computer, on a phone, and with smart RFID stations.
beats.say: It is built for the tool crib, the shop floor and the quality team. It works on a computer, on a phone, and with smart R-F-I-D stations.

beats.text: First, the problems most plants face today.
Problem one: tools are tracked in a paper register or an Excel sheet, so nobody really knows who has the torque wrench right now.
Problem two: a tool whose calibration has expired can still be used on a job, because nothing stops it.
Problem three: tools go missing. They are bought again, and work waits while people search.
And problem four: when an auditor asks for proof, someone spends hours digging through old files.
ToolTrace fixes all four.
Every tool follows one simple cycle: label it, issue it, use it, return it, and calibrate it on time.
You get a live tool board, a calibration lock that cannot be skipped, early warnings for tools at risk, and an audit trail that is always ready.
And all of it is stored safely in your company's own database.
Let's open the app. Staff sign in with a passkey, like a fingerprint or a phone PIN, so there are no passwords to remember. For this demo, I'll sign in as the admin.
This is the tool board. Every tool has its own place, just like a shadow board on the wall.
A solid card means the tool is in the crib. A dotted card means it is out, and shows who has it and when it is due back. Red means overdue.
To issue a tool, I open it, choose the person, and pick when it is due back.
One click, and it is checked out. The board updates straight away.
When a tool comes back, I record its condition. If it is damaged, it goes into quarantine, so nobody takes it by mistake.
Now, calibration. This torque wrench has expired, so ToolTrace has locked it. It cannot be issued until it is calibrated again.
I record the new calibration with its certificate number. The tool is unlocked, and the next due date is worked out for me.
Already have your tool list in Excel? Open Data sources. You can bring in a workbook or a CSV file, or connect MySQL, PostgreSQL or SQL Server.
beats.say: Already have your tool list in Excel? Open Data sources. You can bring in a workbook or a C-S-V file, or connect My S-Q-L, Postgres, or S-Q-L Server.

beats.text: ToolTrace matches the columns for you, and checks every row first. It shows exactly what will be added, and what will be skipped, before anything changes.
On the shop floor, technicians use their phone. They scan the QR label on a tool, and take it in two taps.
beats.say: On the shop floor, technicians use their phone. They scan the Q-R label on a tool, and take it in two taps.

beats.text: No signal? No problem. The app keeps working offline, and syncs as soon as the phone is back online.
At the crib, a smart station reads RFID tags. A technician taps their badge, then the tool, and the board updates live.
beats.say: At the crib, a smart station reads R-F-I-D tags. A technician taps their badge, then the tool, and the board updates live.

beats.text: Insights learns from past check-outs. It points out tools at risk of being lost, and explains the reason in plain words.
Finally, the audit trail records every action: who did what, and when. One click proves that nothing has been changed.
Getting started is simple.
One: import your tool list from Excel, or connect your database.
Two: print a QR label for each tool, and invite your team with a link.
beats.say: Two: print a Q-R label for each tool, and invite your team with a link.

beats.text: Three: start issuing tools. ToolTrace takes care of the rest.
ToolTrace. Every tool, every calibration, always accounted for. Thanks for watching!
